sources.entry: JUMP - Open-source tool that labels every clickable element so you can click, scroll and search any app from the keyboard. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/alvaldes/jump) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.name: JUMP
summary.one_liner: JUMP is a free, open-source macOS tool that labels every clickable element in the focused window so you can click, scroll and search with the keyboard.
use_cases: Click buttons and links in a Mac app without using the mouse
Find and jump to visible text in an app window
Right-click or double-click from the keyboard
Navigate PDFs, terminals and images by recognized on-screen text
summary.what_it_does: JUMP labels every clickable element of the focused window when you press a shortcut (default ⌘⇧Space); typing a label clicks it. Holding ⇧, ⌘ or ⌥ changes the click to right-click, double-click or pointer-move only. A scroll mode uses h j k l, d and u for half pages, and gg and G for the ends, with Tab moving between scrollable areas. Text search finds visible text ignoring case and accents, and optional on-screen text recognition covers terminals, PDFs and images; it is off by default and stays on the Mac. Labels disappear when you switch apps, and shortcuts, label letters, themes, sizes and scroll speed are configurable.
notable: Labels every clickable element in the focused window and types a label to click it
Vim-style scrolling and text search with Tab and Return navigation
Optional on-screen text recognition for terminals, PDFs and images that stays on the Mac
Open source under GPL-3.0, built on ideas and code from Vimac
caveats: Not notarized by Apple yet, so macOS needs a one-time manual confirmation to open it
Needs Accessibility permission to find and click elements in other apps
